Battle of Tinian.fact: The first wave of LVTs, consisting of eight LVTs for White Beach 1 and sixteen for White Beach 2, left the line of departure at 07:17 followed at close intervals by fourteen more waves. Eight LVTs carried a rifle company of about 200 men.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Two pillboxes guarded White Beach _____, which were bypassed by the first waves, but reduced by later ones; fifty dead Japanese were found inside
Battle of Tinian.fact: Company E of the 2nd Battalion, 24th Marines, was first ashore there. It was opposed by a small number of Japanese defenders in crevices and a cave, who were eliminated after a brief action, allowing the rest of the 2nd Battalion and the shore party of the 1341st Engineer Battalion to land unopposed.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Three LVTs were disabled by mines when they ventured inland from _____ 2
Battle of Tinian.fact: Two pillboxes guarded White Beach 2, which were bypassed by the first waves, but reduced by later ones; fifty dead Japanese were found inside. Both beaches had mines; none exploded on White Beach 1, where they had been allowed to deteriorate, but the area around White Beach 2 was sown with anti-boat mines on the beach and anti-personnel mines ashore, which the underwater demolition teams (UDTs), bomb disposal teams and engineers took until 13:37 to clear.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The 4th _____ had trouble negotiating the reefs, potholes and mines on White Beach 2 and was diverted to White Beach 1
Battle of Tinian.fact: The 4th Tank Battalion had trouble negotiating the reefs, potholes and mines on White Beach 2 and was diverted to White Beach 1.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Despite its small size, nearly all vehicles were landed over _____ 1
Battle of Tinian.fact: Both beaches had mines; none exploded on White Beach 1, where they had been allowed to deteriorate, but the area around White Beach 2 was sown with anti-boat mines on the beach and anti-personnel mines ashore, which the underwater demolition teams (UDTs), bomb disposal teams and engineers took until 13:37 to clear. Three LVTs were disabled by mines when they ventured inland from White Beach 2.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: This included the M3 _____ light tanks of Company D with Ronson flamethrowers
Battle of Tinian.fact: This included the M3 Stuart light tanks of Company D with Ronson flamethrowers.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: In the afternoon, _____ A came ashore on White Beach 2 without mishap
Battle of Tinian.fact: This included the M3 Stuart light tanks of Company D with Ronson flamethrowers. In the afternoon, Company A came ashore on White Beach 2 without mishap.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: On White Beach 1 the 2nd _____, 24th Marines, was followed by the 1st Battalion, which was ashore by 08:46, and the 3rd Battalion at 09:25
Battle of Tinian.fact: All three assault battalions were ashore by 08:20. On White Beach 1 the 2nd Battalion, 24th Marines, was followed by the 1st Battalion, which was ashore by 08:46, and the 3rd Battalion at 09:25.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: On White Beach 2, the reserve battalion, the 1st _____, 25th Marines, was ashore by 09:30
Battle of Tinian.fact: All three assault battalions were ashore by 08:20. On White Beach 1 the 2nd Battalion, 24th Marines, was followed by the 1st Battalion, which was ashore by 08:46, and the 3rd Battalion at 09:25.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: DUKWs carrying the artillery began landing at 13:15, the 23rd _____ at 14:00, and the 2nd Marine Division's 1st Battalion, 8th Marines, at 17:00
Battle of Tinian.fact: On White Beach 1 the 2nd Battalion, 24th Marines, was followed by the 1st Battalion, which was ashore by 08:46, and the 3rd Battalion at 09:25. On White Beach 2, the reserve battalion, the 1st Battalion, 25th Marines, was ashore by 09:30.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The planned beachhead was occupied, and the marines strung barbed wire and established fields of fire in anticipation of a _____ counterattack
Battle of Tinian.fact: The planned beachhead was occupied, and the marines strung barbed wire and set up fields of fire in anticipation of a Japanese counterattack.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The 1st Battalion, 50th _____, was already in the vicinity of the American beachhead, and was able to probe the hastily positioned defenses for weaknesses
Battle of Tinian.fact: The 1st Battalion, 50th Infantry Regiment, was already in the vicinity of the American beachhead, and was able to probe the hastily positioned defenses for weaknesses.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The 2nd Battalion in the _____ area was not far away, but could not move until dark, when American aircraft were not in the sky
Battle of Tinian.fact: The 2nd Battalion in the Asiga Bay area was not far away, but could not move until dark, when American aircraft were not in the sky.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Ogata kept the 3rd Battalion in place at _____ in case the Americans made a follow-up landing there
Battle of Tinian.fact: Ogata kept the 3rd Battalion in place at Tinian Town in case the Americans made a follow-up landing there.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Naval troops approached the beachhead from the _____ airfield
Battle of Tinian.fact: Naval troops approached the beachhead from the Ushi Point airfield.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: A furious fight ensued, in which _____ A was reduced to just 30 men, but by 07:00 476 Japanese lay dead
Battle of Tinian.fact: A furious fight ensued, in which Company A was reduced to just 30 men, but by 07:00 476 Japanese lay dead. About 200 Japanese soldiers broke through the lines of Company K, 25th Marines, and divided into two groups.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: In the center of the _____ line another attack developed at the boundary between the 24th and 25th Marines
Battle of Tinian.fact: At around 02:00 on 25 July, a force of about 600 Japanese sailors encountered the 1st Battalion, 24th Marines, on the left of the American beachhead, and charged into machine gun, mortar, rifle and 37 mm antitank gun canister shot fire. In the center of the American line another attack developed at the boundary between the 24th and 25th Marines.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: About 200 _____ soldiers broke through the lines of Company K, 25th Marines, and divided into two groups
Battle of Tinian.fact: At around 02:00 on 25 July, a force of about 600 Japanese sailors encountered the 1st Battalion, 24th Marines, on the left of the American beachhead, and charged into machine gun, mortar, rifle and 37 mm antitank gun canister shot fire. A furious fight ensued, in which Company A was reduced to just 30 men, but by 07:00 476 Japanese lay dead.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: One group attacked _____ D, 14th Marines
Battle of Tinian.fact: One group attacked Battery D, 14th Marines. About 100 dead Japanese were found in the area; two men of Battery D were killed.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The attack was halted with the help of _____ .50 caliber machine gun fire from Batteries E and F. Company C of the 8th Marines was sent to their aid, but found the situation in hand
Battle of Tinian.fact: The attack was halted with the help of Browning .50 caliber machine gun fire from Batteries E and F. Company C of the 8th Marines was sent to their aid, but found the situation in hand.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: About 100 dead _____ were found in the area; two men of Battery D were killed
Battle of Tinian.fact: About 200 Japanese soldiers broke through the lines of Company K, 25th Marines, and divided into two groups. About 100 dead Japanese were found in the area; two men of Battery D were killed.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The attack in the center cost the _____ about 500 dead, most of whom were from the 1st Battalion, 135th Infantry Regiment
Battle of Tinian.fact: About 100 dead Japanese were found in the area; two men of Battery D were killed. The attack in the center cost the Japanese about 500 dead, most of whom were from the 1st Battalion, 135th Infantry Regiment.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: On the right, the 23rd _____ were attacked by five or six Japanese tanks, accompanied by infantry of the 1st and 2nd Battalions, 50th Infantry Regiment, and the 1st Battalion, 135th Infantry Regiment
Battle of Tinian.fact: On the right, the 23rd Marines were attacked by five or six Japanese tanks, accompanied by infantry of the 1st and 2nd Battalions, 50th Infantry Regiment, and the 1st Battalion, 135th Infantry Regiment. The Japanese infantry charged the lines of the 2nd battalion, 23rd Marines, and 2nd Battalion, 25th Marines.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The Japanese infantry charged the lines of the 2nd battalion, 23rd _____, and 2nd Battalion, 25th Marines
Battle of Tinian.fact: On the right, the 23rd Marines were attacked by five or six Japanese tanks, accompanied by infantry of the 1st and 2nd Battalions, 50th Infantry Regiment, and the 1st Battalion, 135th Infantry Regiment. The Japanese infantry charged the lines of the 2nd battalion, 23rd Marines, and 2nd Battalion, 25th Marines.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The moonless night was lit up by _____ star shells
Battle of Tinian.fact: The moonless night was lit up by Navy star shells.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Some broke through their lines, only to encounter the 1st _____, 23rd Marines
Battle of Tinian.fact: The Japanese infantry charged the lines of the 2nd battalion, 23rd Marines, and 2nd Battalion, 25th Marines. Some broke through their lines, only to encounter the 1st Battalion, 23rd Marines.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: In the morning, 267 _____ dead were counted in this sector
Battle of Tinian.fact: Five Japanese tanks were knocked out by bazookas, 75 mm halftracks and 37 mm antitank guns. The Japanese infantry charged the lines of the 2nd battalion, 23rd Marines, and 2nd Battalion, 25th Marines.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: In all, the counterattack cost _____ about 1,200 dead
Battle of Tinian.fact: In all, the counterattack cost Ogata about 1,200 dead.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: In the meantime, the rest of the 2nd _____ began landing
Battle of Tinian.fact: In the meantime, the rest of the 2nd Marine Division began landing.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: On their right, the 2nd _____, 8th Marines, reached the Ushi Point airfield, and the 24th Marines reached airfield No
Battle of Tinian.fact: As they moved north along the coast through terrain characterized by coral rocks and thick undergrowth, the 1st Battalion, 8th Marines, was held up by a force of 20 to 25 Japanese that it took until 11:30 to overcome. On their right, the 2nd Battalion, 8th Marines, reached the Ushi Point airfield, and the 24th Marines reached airfield No.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The 25th _____ was confronted by the most formidable obstacle of the day, Mount Maga, which was captured with a double envelopment
Battle of Tinian.fact: As they moved north along the coast through terrain characterized by coral rocks and thick undergrowth, the 1st Battalion, 8th Marines, was held up by a force of 20 to 25 Japanese that it took until 11:30 to overcome. On their right, the 2nd Battalion, 8th Marines, reached the Ushi Point airfield, and the 24th Marines reached airfield No.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The following day, the 25th _____ captured the steeper and more imposing Mount Lasso without opposition, as the Japanese had pulled out during the night
Battle of Tinian.fact: As they moved north along the coast through terrain characterized by coral rocks and thick undergrowth, the 1st Battalion, 8th Marines, was held up by a force of 20 to 25 Japanese that it took until 11:30 to overcome. On their right, the 2nd Battalion, 8th Marines, reached the Ushi Point airfield, and the 24th Marines reached airfield No.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The marines pressed forward on 27 and 28 July against sporadic _____ resistance
Battle of Tinian.fact: The following day, the 25th Marines captured the steeper and more imposing Mount Lasso without opposition, as the Japanese had pulled out during the night. The marines pressed forward on 27 and 28 July against sporadic Japanese resistance.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: A typhoon in the _____ caused heavy swells
Battle of Tinian.fact: A typhoon in the Philippine Sea caused heavy swells.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: On 13 _____, she was pulled off the reef and towed to Tanapag Harbor, where she was beached
Battle of Tinian.fact: On 13 August, she was pulled off the reef and towed to Tanapag Harbor, where she was beached.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: A control craft, LCC-25473, was washed up on the reef at _____ 1, but was salvaged the following day
Battle of Tinian.fact: A control craft, LCC-25473, was washed up on the reef at White Beach 1, but was salvaged the following day. The one at White Beach 1 broached and the one at White Beach 2 broke in two.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The one at _____ 1 broached and the one at White Beach 2 broke in two
Battle of Tinian.fact: A control craft, LCC-25473, was washed up on the reef at White Beach 1, but was salvaged the following day. The one at White Beach 1 broached and the one at White Beach 2 broke in two.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The pontoon causeways were damaged on the night of 29 _____
Battle of Tinian.fact: The pontoon causeways were damaged on the night of 29 July. The White Beach 1 causeway was restored to service on 31 July, only to broach again.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The White Beach 1 causeway was restored to service on 31 _____, only to broach again
Battle of Tinian.fact: The pontoon causeways were damaged on the night of 29 July. The White Beach 1 causeway was restored to service on 31 July, only to broach again.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: With the _____ airfield in American hands, the 121st Naval Construction Battalion commenced its repair on 27 July, filling in the bomb and shell craters
Battle of Tinian.fact: With the Ushi Point airfield in American hands, the 121st Naval Construction Battalion commenced its repair on 27 July, filling in the bomb and shell craters.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: By that evening, an airstrip _____ (760 m) long and 150 feet (46 m) wide was ready for use, and it was fully restored to its 4,700-foot (1,400 m) length the next day
Battle of Tinian.fact: By that evening, an airstrip 2,500 feet (760 m) long and 150 feet (46 m) wide was ready for use, and it was fully restored to its 4,700-foot (1,400 m) length the next day.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: On 29 _____, a P-47 landed and took off again
Battle of Tinian.fact: The White Beach 1 causeway was restored to service on 31 July, only to broach again. With the Ushi Point airfield in American hands, the 121st Naval Construction Battalion commenced its repair on 27 July, filling in the bomb and shell craters.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Hill summoned the 9th _____ from Eniwetok and its Douglas C-47 Skytrains, together with the Curtiss C-46 Commandos of VMR-252, delivered 33,000 rations from Saipan on 31 July
Battle of Tinian.fact: Hill summoned the 9th Troop Carrier Squadron from Eniwetok and its Douglas C-47 Skytrains, together with the Curtiss C-46 Commandos of VMR-252, delivered 33,000 rations from Saipan on 31 July.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: One important task for the DUKWs was hauling ammunition from the ammunition ships SS _____, which arrived off Tinian on 26 July, and MS Sea Witch, which arrived the following day
Battle of Tinian.fact: One important task for the DUKWs was hauling ammunition from the ammunition ships SS Rockland Victory, which arrived off Tinian on 26 July, and MS Sea Witch, which arrived the following day.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: A gasoline shortage was averted by the capture of _____ stocks
Battle of Tinian.fact: A gasoline shortage was averted by the capture of Japanese stocks.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: On 30 July the 24th Marines occupied _____ and the 25th Marines overran airfield no
Battle of Tinian.fact: On 30 July the 24th Marines occupied Tinian Town and the 25th Marines overran airfield no.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The land mines were cleared away, and LCTs began landing on _____
Battle of Tinian.fact: The land mines were cleared away, and LCTs began landing on Green Beach.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The water off the south pier was not deep enough to allow LSTs to dock there, so pontoon causeways were brought from White Beach _____ and Saipan, allowing the first LST to dock on 4 August
Battle of Tinian.fact: The water off the south pier was not deep enough to allow LSTs to dock there, so pontoon causeways were brought from White Beach 1 and Saipan, allowing the first LST to dock on 4 August.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The beach between the two piers was cleared of land mines by 5 _____, and was resurfaced with coral, allowing up to fifteen LCMs to beach there simultaneously
Battle of Tinian.fact: The water off the south pier was not deep enough to allow LSTs to dock there, so pontoon causeways were brought from White Beach 1 and Saipan, allowing the first LST to dock on 4 August. The beach between the two piers was cleared of land mines by 5 August, and was resurfaced with coral, allowing up to fifteen LCMs to beach there simultaneously.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: On the evening of 30 July, _____ ordered his divisions to occupy the coastline between Lalo and Mapo Points, and annihilate the remaining Japanese forces
Battle of Tinian.fact: On the evening of 30 July, Schmidt ordered his divisions to occupy the coastline between Lalo and Mapo Points, and annihilate the remaining Japanese forces.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Kakuta sent his last radio message to _____ that day
Battle of Tinian.fact: Kakuta sent his last radio message to Tokyo that day.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The rugged terrain hampered the tanks but the flamethrower tanks of Company D, 4th _____, were adept at burning sections of undergrowth where Japanese soldiers tried to hide
Battle of Tinian.fact: The rugged terrain hampered the tanks but the flamethrower tanks of Company D, 4th Tank Battalion, were adept at burning sections of undergrowth where Japanese soldiers tried to hide. The accompanying tanks of Company C, 4th Tank Battalion, were engaged by a concealed Japanese 47 mm antitank gun, which scored six hits on one tank.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The accompanying tanks of _____ C, 4th Tank Battalion, were engaged by a concealed Japanese 47 mm antitank gun, which scored six hits on one tank
Battle of Tinian.fact: The rugged terrain hampered the tanks but the flamethrower tanks of Company D, 4th Tank Battalion, were adept at burning sections of undergrowth where Japanese soldiers tried to hide. The accompanying tanks of Company C, 4th Tank Battalion, were engaged by a concealed Japanese 47 mm antitank gun, which scored six hits on one tank.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: As the 23rd _____ approached the plateau, they came under intense small arms fire from a small village and the cliff face
Battle of Tinian.fact: As the 23rd Marines approached the plateau, they came under intense small arms fire from a small village and the cliff face.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Although also penetrated, it too remained operational, and this time the target was spotted, and engaged by tanks that destroyed the gun and machine-gunned twenty _____ crewmen who tried to escape
Battle of Tinian.fact: Although also penetrated, it too remained operational, and this time the target was spotted, and engaged by tanks that destroyed the gun and machine-gunned twenty Japanese crewmen who tried to escape. Meanwhile, the 8th Marines made their way onto the plateau, where vegetation covered caves and fissures where Japanese riflemen and machine gunners lurked.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Meanwhile, the 8th _____ made their way onto the plateau, where vegetation covered caves and fissures where Japanese riflemen and machine gunners lurked
Battle of Tinian.fact: Meanwhile, the 8th Marines made their way onto the plateau, where vegetation covered caves and fissures where Japanese riflemen and machine gunners lurked.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: While the vegetation concealed them from observation by the _____, it also restricted their own fields of view
Battle of Tinian.fact: While the vegetation concealed them from observation by the Americans, it also restricted their own fields of view.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations

Battle of Tinian.fact: Meanwhile, the 8th Marines made their way onto the plateau, where vegetation covered caves and fissures where Japanese riflemen and machine gunners lurked. Engineers removed the mines, allowing tanks to proceed up the road and destroy Japanese positions, while the accompanying infantry battled their way through the brush.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations

Battle of Tinian.fact: Engineers removed the mines, allowing tanks to proceed up the road and destroy Japanese positions, while the accompanying infantry battled their way through the brush. At 16:50, Company A reached the top.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Five minutes later they were joined by a platoon from _____ E, following up the road, was attacked by between 75 and 100 Japanese, who were eventually repelled
Battle of Tinian.fact: Five minutes later they were joined by a platoon from Company C. Company E, following up the road, was attacked by between 75 and 100 Japanese, who were eventually repelled.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: During the night, the _____ attempted to cut off the Americans on the summit
Battle of Tinian.fact: Five minutes later they were joined by a platoon from Company C. Company E, following up the road, was attacked by between 75 and 100 Japanese, who were eventually repelled. During the night, the Japanese attempted to cut off the Americans on the summit.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: At 05:15 the marines' positions were attacked by more than 600 _____ soldiers and sailors
Battle of Tinian.fact: During the night, the Japanese attempted to cut off the Americans on the summit. At 05:15 the marines' positions were attacked by more than 600 Japanese soldiers and sailors.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: An hour later, the 8th _____ had 74 casualties and 200 Japanese were dead
Battle of Tinian.fact: At 05:15 the marines' positions were attacked by more than 600 Japanese soldiers and sailors. An hour later, the 8th Marines had 74 casualties and 200 Japanese were dead.

Battle of Tinian.fact: Lolo Point, the southernmost tip of the island, was reached at 18:00 on 1 August, and 55 minutes later, Schmidt declared that organized resistance had ended, and the island was secure.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Nonetheless, that night, the 6th _____ were attacked by a poorly coordinated force of about 150 Japanese soldiers and sailors
Battle of Tinian.fact: An hour later, the 8th Marines had 74 casualties and 200 Japanese were dead. Nonetheless, that night, the 6th Marines were attacked by a poorly coordinated force of about 150 Japanese soldiers and sailors.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: According to _____ prisoners, Ogata had burned the regimental colors and gathered as many men as he could for a counterattack
Battle of Tinian.fact: Nonetheless, that night, the 6th Marines were attacked by a poorly coordinated force of about 150 Japanese soldiers and sailors. According to Japanese prisoners, Ogata had burned the regimental colors and gathered as many men as he could for a counterattack.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The following morning 124 _____ dead were counted, many of whom had died by their own hand, but Ogata's body was never identified

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Some sources state _____ committed suicide
Battle of Tinian.fact: According to Japanese prisoners, Ogata had burned the regimental colors and gathered as many men as he could for a counterattack. The following morning 124 Japanese dead were counted, many of whom had died by their own hand, but Ogata's body was never identified.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The 4th _____ lost 182 killed, 844 wounded and 20 missing, a total of 1,046
Battle of Tinian.fact: The 4th Marine Division lost 182 killed, 844 wounded and 20 missing, a total of 1,046.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The dead included two men who were posthumously awarded the Medal of Honor for using their bodies to protect their comrades from hand grenades: Private Joseph W. Ozbourn and _____
Battle of Tinian.answer: Private First Class Robert L. Wilson
Battle of Tinian.fact: The dead included two men who were posthumously awarded the Medal of Honor for using their bodies to protect their comrades from hand grenades: Private Joseph W. Ozbourn and Private First Class Robert L. Wilson.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: By 10 August, _____ casualties included 404 taken prisoner and 5,745 dead that were buried by the Americans
Battle of Tinian.fact: By 10 August, Japanese casualties included 404 taken prisoner and 5,745 dead that were buried by the Americans. The operation was much less difficult than Saipan; the nearest American base was just 5 miles (8.0 km) away, not over a thousand; the Japanese garrison was smaller; the ratio of attackers to defenders was greater; the terrain was less formidable; intelligence was more accurate; and the preliminary naval and aerial bombardment more protracted.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: DUKWs were still able to operate when landing craft could not, and _____ recommended that DUKWs replace LCVPs on the Navy's attack cargo ships
Battle of Tinian.fact: DUKWs were still able to operate when landing craft could not, and Hill recommended that DUKWs replace LCVPs on the Navy's attack cargo ships.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: For their part, the surprised _____ defenders made the further mistake by following standard doctrine and fell into the trap set by the recently landed American attackers
Battle of Tinian.fact: For their part, the surprised Japanese defenders made the further mistake by following standard doctrine and fell into the trap set by the recently landed American attackers. Believing that this was the only way to eject the Americans, the Japanese incurred high casualties by assembling in the open to conduct fruitless counterattacks to retake the landing beach, all of which were anticipated by the Americans who were well prepared and could bring their superior firepower to bear.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations

Battle of Tinian.fact: The 8th Marines assumed responsibility for the whole 2nd Marine Division's sector two days later, allowing the rest of the division to return to Saipan for rest and reorganization.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: On 10 _____ it took over the 4th Marine Division's sector as well, so it could return to Hawaii
Battle of Tinian.fact: On 10 August it took over the 4th Marine Division's sector as well, so it could return to Hawaii. Major General James L. Underhill was appointed Island Commander on 1 August 1944.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: Major General James L. Underhill was appointed Island Commander on 1 August _____
Battle of Tinian.fact: Major General James L. Underhill was appointed Island Commander on 1 August 1944.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: He was succeeded by _____ on 28 November
Battle of Tinian.answer: Brigadier General Frederick V. H. Kimble
Battle of Tinian.fact: He was succeeded by Brigadier General Frederick V. H. Kimble on 28 November.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: The 8th _____ patroled the island, mopping up Japanese holdouts
Battle of Tinian.fact: The 8th Marines patroled the island, mopping up Japanese holdouts. On 25 October, the 8th Marines joined the rest of the 2nd Marine Division on Saipan, leaving the 1st Battalion behind on Tinian.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations
Battle of Tinian.question: On 25 _____, the 8th Marines joined the rest of the 2nd Marine Division on Saipan, leaving the 1st Battalion behind on Tinian
Battle of Tinian.fact: On 25 October, the 8th Marines joined the rest of the 2nd Marine Division on Saipan, leaving the 1st Battalion behind on Tinian.

Battle of Tinian.subject: International Relations

BRICS.question: China also launched its alternative to SWIFT: the Cross-_____, which enables financial institutions worldwide to send and receive information about financial transactions
BRICS.fact: === BRICS payment system === At the 2015 BRICS summit in Russia, ministers from the BRICS states initiated consultations for a payment system that would be an alternative to the SWIFT system.  The stated goal was to initially move to settlements in national currencies.  The Central Bank of Russia highlighted the main benefits as backup and redundancy in case there were disruptions to the SWIFT system.  China also launched its alternative to SWIFT: the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System, which enables financial institutions worldwide to send and receive information about financial transactions.  India also has its alternative Structured Financial Messaging System (SFMS), as do Russia SPFS and Brazil Pix.  === Potential common currency and BRICS Bridge === BRICS countries committed to study the feasibility of a new common currency or similar, at the 2023 BRICS summit in South Africa.  Fair and easier international trade, as well as a major reduction in costs of transactions, would be some of the reasons for the countries to forge a currency union

In parallel with institutional initiatives, a proposal has been put forward for a supranational currency known as UNIT, designed by the International Reserve and Investment Asset System (IRIAS). BRICS.fact: BRICS is an intergovernmental organization comprising ten countries: Brazil, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia and the United Arab Emirates.  Its conceptual origins were articulated by Russian foreign minister Yevgeny Primakov in 1998, and can be traced to informal forums and dialogue groups such as RIC (Russia, India, and China) and IBSA (India, Brazil, and South Africa).  BRIC was originally a term coined by British economist Jim O'Neill, and later championed by his employer Goldman Sachs in 2001, to designate a group of emerging markets.  The bloc's inaugural summit was held in 2009 and featured the founding countries of Brazil, Russia, India, and China; they adopted the acronym BRIC and formed an informal diplomatic group where their governments could meet annually at formal summits and coordinate multilateral policies.  South Africa joined the organization in September 2010, which was then renamed BRICS, and attended the third summit in 2011 as a full member.  Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, and the United Arab Emirates attended their first summit as member states in 2024 in Russia
